# Kestrel Ridge Health

> Kestrel Ridge Health is ophthalmology staffing software from an Ohio company. It
> forecasts ophthalmic technician workload by clinic session, using measured technician-minutes per
> visit type rather than a fixed technician-to-provider ratio, and plans core plus
> float staffing across sites. Validation to date is on synthetic data only; the
> company is pre-revenue and makes no customer outcome, ROI, or savings claims.

## What it is
- A staffing-forecast tool for ophthalmology groups and multi-location eye clinics:
  it predicts how much technician time each clinic session needs, so administrators
  can staff to real workload instead of a flat ratio.
- A deterministic solver assigns staff under hard constraints; a human approves
  every consequential decision. The method and its limits are published.
- Designed for ophthalmology administrators, operations directors, and practice
  managers at multi-site eye-care groups. Not a scheduling app for individual
  clinicians.

## The clinical problem it addresses
- Most eye clinics staff by a fixed technician-to-provider ratio (e.g., 2:1).
  That ratio ignores visit-type mix: cataract follow-ups vs. comprehensive exams
  vs. contact-lens fits require very different technician time.
- When session mix shifts (adding surgical volume, opening a new site, onboarding
  a new provider), a flat ratio over- or under-staffs. The result is unnecessary
  overtime, call-offs, or patient throughput bottlenecks.
- KRH models each visit type's measured technician-minutes and forecasts session
  demand before the schedule finalizes, so staffing decisions are data-driven.

## Phase Zero pilot offering
- KRH's offering is a Phase Zero diagnostic with a defined scope. KRH works with one or two clinic sites to import
  historical scheduling data, map visit types to technician-time estimates, run
  the forecast model against past sessions, and report the gap between modeled
  staffing and actual staffing.
- Phase Zero does not require full production deployment. It is designed so an
  operations director can evaluate the forecast method with real clinic data before
  committing to a broader rollout.
- Buyers: ophthalmology group administrators, operations directors, CFOs, and
  medical directors at multi-location eye clinics.

Nine questions about one typical session give a Low, Elevated or High band for six areas of technician coverage, with the rule behind each. Rule-based screening, not a benchmark or forecast. Answers stay in the browser.
- [How It Works](https://kestrelridgehealth.com/how-it-works/): the forecasting workflow step by step.

- [Technician shortage and session variance](https://kestrelridgehealth.com/technician-shortage-session-variance/): the operational problem in detail.
- [Same-day ophthalmology staffing](https://kestrelridgehealth.com/same-day-ophthalmology-staffing/): handling same-day add-ons without ratio blowout.
- [Call-off coverage for eye clinics](https://kestrelridgehealth.com/call-off-coverage-eye-clinics/): planned float coverage vs. reactive scrambling.
- [Ophthalmology staffing software compared](https://kestrelridgehealth.com/ophthalmology-staffing-software-compared/): the five ways eye clinics plan technician staffing, what each can and cannot see, and when Kestrel Ridge Health is the wrong choice.

- [Contact](https://kestrelridgehealth.com/contact/): start a Phase Zero conversation.

## Honest scope
- Pre-revenue. No live customer deployments disclosed.
- All accuracy figures are from synthetic data, not real patient or clinic data.
- No claim of HIPAA compliance or any regulatory certification.
- The company does not guarantee staffing outcomes, cost savings, or improved patient throughput.
- The forecast model is a planning tool; it does not replace clinical judgment or
  human staffing decisions.
